prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-29. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.39 |
| Retained earnings       | 49,956M |
| Current liabilities     | 18,377M |
| Current assets          | 25,508M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 52,061M |
| Total liabilities       | 57,728M |
| Total assets            | 110,429M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,842M |
| Revenue                 | 11,164M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-29, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided metrics indicate moderate leverage (total liabilities/equity of ~1.11), adequate liquidity (current ratio of 1.39), and solid profitability (EBIT margin ~16.5%) for an established firm with a large retained-earnings buffer. These factors collectively support an upper-medium-grade rating in the single-A category, though the absence of interest-coverage or cash-flow data prevents a higher assessment.
DECISION: A-
